m4-t1.introduction: A second way to understand “Headcount, FTE and movement reconciliation”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: People, contracted hours and FTE are different units
sections.explanation: The snapshot fixture has 24 full-time and six half-time contracts using a 40-hour weekly standard. It is separate from the period turnover example.

items.label: Headcount
items.detail: 30 people are active under the snapshot’s inclusion rule.

items.label: Contracted FTE
items.detail: 1,080 ÷ 40 = 27 FTE under this specific standard.

sections.takeaway: FTE is a stated capacity convention, not a score of personal worth or productivity.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: The movement bridge depends on the boundary
sections.explanation: Opening plus joiners minus leavers is complete only when other relevant movements are absent. Department transfers require extra terms.

items.label: Opening population
items.detail: Fix the snapshot date and counting scope.

items.label: Add entries
items.detail: Include valid joins and department transfers in where relevant.

items.label: Subtract exits
items.detail: Include departures and department transfers out where relevant.

items.label: Reconcile closing
items.detail: Explain the difference between the expected and observed count.

sections.takeaway: Use effective dates and defined employment spells; do not silently mix people and events.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 2. Reconcile movements at the right boundary

sections.title: Stable headcount does not mean stable capacity
sections.explanation: Hours, skill coverage, availability and workload can change even when the number of people does not.

items.label: Contracted capacity
items.detail: Use a declared hours basis and FTE standard.

items.label: Skills and access
items.detail: Check whether the required work can actually be covered.

items.label: Availability
items.detail: Consider appropriate leave, training and shift constraints.

items.label: Service requirement
items.detail: Match assumptions to workload and quality standards.

sections.takeaway: Do not treat overtime or every paid hour as permanently sustainable productive capacity.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Can 30 headcount and 27 FTE both be correct for the same snapshot?
checkpoint.answer: Yes. Headcount counts people; FTE divides included hours by a stated full-time standard. The units and inclusion rules differ.

m4-t2.introduction: A second way to understand “Turnover, retention and absence”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Turnover and retention do not share a denominator
sections.explanation: The lesson’s 100 opening, 120 closing, 11 exits and 92 retained opening members are consistent with one illustrative breakdown: 31 joiners, eight opening-cohort exits and three joiner exits. Change a count to explore the definitions.

items.label: Opening
items.detail: The cohort present at the start of the stated period.

items.label: Joiners
items.detail: People entering during the same period, before any later exit.

items.label: Leavers
items.detail: Opening-cohort and new-joiner exits together.

items.label: Closing
items.detail: Opening plus joiners minus all included exits.

sections.takeaway: Turnover uses all period exits over approximate average headcount; retention follows only the fixed opening cohort.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Absence requires scheduled exposure
sections.explanation: The synthetic example has 80 included absent scheduled hours out of 2,000 scheduled hours. The inclusion policy still needs to be stated.

items.label: Define inclusion
items.detail: State which absence and approved-leave types count.

items.label: Count absent exposure
items.detail: Use included scheduled hours actually absent.

items.label: Count eligible exposure
items.detail: Use total scheduled hours under the same population and period.

items.label: Calculate and qualify
items.detail: Show the rate, counts and policy limitations together.

sections.takeaway: 80 ÷ 2,000 = 4%; an aggregate absence rate is not a diagnosis or evidence of misconduct.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Small counts can make large-looking rate changes
sections.explanation: A rate needs counts, a denominator, comparable periods and a confidentiality review to be interpreted responsibly.

items.label: Size and uncertainty
items.detail: One event can strongly change a small group’s percentage.

items.label: Comparable context
items.detail: Check season, tenure mix and organisational change.

items.label: Safe reporting
items.detail: Review tiny groups and indirect identification before sharing.

items.label: Proportionate action
items.detail: Consult qualified HR owners and test a supportive process response.

sections.takeaway: Use aggregate signals to investigate systems, not to diagnose or publicly label individuals.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 3. Interpret rates with counts and context

checkpoint.question: In the initial example, why is retention 92% rather than one minus the 10% turnover rate?
checkpoint.answer: Retention follows the 92 remaining members of the original 100. Turnover divides all 11 exits by approximate average headcount 110. The populations and denominators differ.

m4-t3.introduction: A second way to understand “Demand, supply and workforce scenarios”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: A demand assumption changes the required FTE
sections.explanation: The independent capacity fixture uses 800 cases per productive FTE. Workloads of 8,800, 9,600 and 10,400 imply three demand scenarios.

items.label: Lower workload
items.detail: 8,800 cases ÷ 800 cases per productive FTE.

items.label: Base workload
items.detail: 9,600 cases ÷ 800 cases per productive FTE.

items.label: Higher workload
items.detail: 10,400 cases ÷ 800 cases per productive FTE.

sections.takeaway: These are synthetic planning scenarios, not staffing promises or permission to intensify work. Check skills, service quality and sustainable capacity.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Supply is a dated set of assumptions
sections.explanation: Starting capacity, expected additions, departures, transfers and availability need distinct entries. An accepted offer is not guaranteed capacity.

items.label: Start with current capacity
items.detail: Use the relevant skill and availability basis.

items.label: Add confirmed changes
items.detail: Record joins, transfers and changed hours with timing.

items.label: Apply losses once
items.detail: Account for departures or reduced availability explicitly.

items.label: Show uncertainty
items.detail: Separate confirmed, proposed and delayed scenarios.

sections.takeaway: Avoid subtracting an expected exit twice or counting an unapproved role as confirmed supply.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: A workforce gap has more than one possible response
sections.explanation: Hiring, mobility, training and process changes have different lead times, costs and quality effects.

items.label: Recruit
items.detail: Account for approval, time to join and onboarding.

items.label: Develop or move
items.detail: Check skills, fair access and the effect on the sending team.

items.label: Improve the process
items.detail: Test work design, demand smoothing or avoidable rework.

items.label: Review the plan
items.detail: Update assumptions using observed workload and service quality.

sections.takeaway: Choose a proportionate option with an owner, review trigger and employment-policy safeguards.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: If a candidate accepts an offer, should the plan count their full productive capacity as available immediately?
checkpoint.answer: No. Joining, onboarding, skill and availability assumptions must be explicit. Use confirmed changes and separate uncertain scenarios.

m4-pb3.introduction: A second way to understand “Project Block 3 — Workforce metrics and scenario plan”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Workforce metrics and scenario plan: connect the question to evidence
sections.explanation: A reconciled headcount/FTE bridge and capacity scenarios that keep turnover, retention and absence denominators distinct.

items.label: Question
items.detail: A reconciled headcount/FTE bridge and capacity scenarios that keep turnover, retention and absence denominators distinct.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Use the original practice material with explicit provenance.

items.label: Decision
items.detail: Explain a bounded recommendation and the evidence that could change it.

sections.takeaway: The app records reading and quizzes; external project submission, verification and marking remain with the institution.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Keep synthetic fixtures and authority boundaries separate
sections.explanation: The practice tables are independent examples, not linked real employee records. Use the original inputs and log every deliberate scenario change.

items.label: Provenance
items.detail: Identify the fixture, grain, period and original source copy.

items.label: Separation
items.detail: Do not join independent populations as if they were one company dataset.

items.label: Permission
items.detail: Use synthetic inputs and the institution-approved submission route.

items.label: Honest context
items.detail: Do not report simulated interviews, approvals or outcomes as live events.

sections.takeaway: No real personal dataset, paid tool or live organisational access is required or authorised by this project.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Reserve time for correction, not only construction
sections.explanation: The original work-plan table supplies the timing. This map groups the work into a review loop without changing those allocations.

items.label: Frame
items.detail: Read the decision and inspect source boundaries.

items.label: Build
items.detail: Create the required artefacts with traceable formulas or decisions.

items.label: Check
items.detail: Reproduce the headline and inspect assumptions and safeguards.

items.label: Review and revise
items.detail: Use peer or self-review and keep a change log.

items.label: Explain and submit
items.detail: Finish the recommendation, disclosure and evidence index.

sections.takeaway: A first draft is not a finished artefact; retain the comment and your response after review.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Organise the workforce metrics and scenario plan submission
sections.explanation: These groups help you locate evidence; the full numbered submission checklist above still defines every required component.

items.label: Snapshot and FTE
items.detail: Use the declared 40-hour standard and show department summaries.

items.label: Movement bridge
items.detail: Reconcile joins, exits and transfers at the correct boundary.

items.label: Metric cards
items.detail: Check turnover, opening-cohort retention and scheduled-hours absence separately.

items.label: Capacity scenarios
items.detail: Keep base, low and high assumptions and recruitment lead time visible.

items.label: Proportionate recommendation
items.detail: Compare hiring with a responsible process or mobility alternative.

sections.takeaway: A public portfolio copy must be safe and clearly labelled; it is not a substitute for the editable institutional submission.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Keep snapshot capacity and period rates separate
sections.explanation: The 30-person contract snapshot and the opening/closing workforce period are independent teaching fixtures. They are not records from one linked workforce.

items.label: Snapshot · 27 FTE
items.detail: 24 full-time plus six half-time contracts give 30 people and 27 FTE under the stated standard.

items.label: Period · 10% turnover
items.detail: Average headcount = (100 + 120) ÷ 2 = 110; all 11 exits ÷ 110 × 100 = 10% for this period.

items.label: Opening cohort · 92% retention
items.detail: 92 original members remain out of 100 opening members; joiners do not enter this denominator.

sections.takeaway: People, contracted FTE and event rates have different units and boundaries. Turnover and fixed-cohort retention are not complements.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Follow the original rubric and its evidence standard
sections.explanation: The original block or capstone marks, performance anchors and institutional award conditions are unchanged.

items.label: Correctness and reproducibility
items.detail: Trace the method and results to the declared source and definitions.

items.label: Judgement and safeguards
items.detail: Show uncertainty, appropriate authority and safe handling.

items.label: Clarity, evidence and reflection
items.detail: Make claims inspectable and explain corrections.

sections.takeaway: These panels and animations do not calculate marks, approve projects or award an external credential.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Review the recommendation from a challenger’s view
sections.explanation: A reviewer should be able to trace a claim, test an assumption and understand which action needs another role’s approval.

items.label: Trace a headline
items.detail: Find the calculation or artefact behind the main claim.

items.label: Challenge an assumption
items.detail: Ask what missing evidence could reverse the action.

items.label: Check authority
items.detail: Name who is permitted to approve a consequential decision.

items.label: Inspect sharing
items.detail: Choose evidence that can safely appear in the public version.

sections.takeaway: Keep the actual review comment and your correction or explanation instead of claiming a review that never happened.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Explain assistance without outsourcing judgement
sections.explanation: Complete the original AI-use statement even when no AI was used. Tool help must not fabricate records, sources or experience.

items.label: Name tools or none
items.detail: State the actual assistance and permitted synthetic inputs.

items.label: Record your checks
items.detail: Explain accepted, changed and rejected suggestions and independent verification.

items.label: Own the work
items.detail: Describe your contribution, judgement and responsibility for the final claims.

sections.takeaway: Do not upload real employee, candidate, student or credential data to public AI tools; follow exam restrictions separately.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: An extension tests an assumption after the core is complete
sections.explanation: The optional extension is not required for full marks. Keep the original work and distinguish a changed scenario from an observation.

items.label: Complete the core
items.detail: Finish the required evidence and safeguards first.

items.label: A changed productive-capacity assumption
items.detail: Explain the new gap while keeping people and FTE units distinct.

items.label: Compare and document
items.detail: Show what changed, which conclusion depends on it and what remains unknown.

sections.takeaway: More complexity does not improve a submission if the reasoning and safeguards cannot be reproduced.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Can 10% turnover be subtracted from 100% to obtain the project’s retention rate?
checkpoint.answer: No. The period turnover denominator is approximate average headcount 110 and includes all 11 exits. Retention follows 92 remaining members of the fixed opening cohort of 100, so it is 92%.
